nodes.name: Ti mesh pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Ti mesh with size of 15 mm×10 mm×0.2 mm was washed ultrasonically with acetone, absolute ethanol and deionized water for 10 min in sequence, and then soaked in 50 mL 10% H2C2O4 at 90°C for 60 min to achieve chemical etching process for the surface of Ti substrate. The substrate after etching was cleaned ultrasonically in deionized water to finally obtain Ti mesh with porous surface (referred as Ti).
nodes.source_text: Firstly, Ti mesh with size of 15 mm×10 mm×0.2 mm was washed ultrasonically with acetone... to finally obtain Ti mesh with porous surface

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Mo precursor
nodes.procedure: Ti mesh after etching was used as the working electrode, a Pt electrode as the counter electrode and a Hg/Hg2SO4 electrode as the reference. The electrolyte was composed of 0.01 M (NH4)2MoO4 and 0.002 M H2SO4. The electrodeposition was carried out at the constant potential of -1.43 V versus Hg/Hg2SO4 for 200 s to obtain Ti-supported molybdenum oxide precursor.
nodes.source_text: The electrodeposition was carried out at the constant potential of -1.43 V versus Hg/Hg2SO4 for 200 s...

nodes.name: Thermal oxidation to MoO3/Ti
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, the precursor was transferred into a crucible and heated to 400°C in a muffle furnace with a heating rate of 10°C min^-1 in ambient atmosphere. After heating at 400°C for 5 h, the precursor was successfully transformed into MoO3/Ti.

nodes.name: Ir precursor solution preparation
nodes.procedure: 11 mg (NH4)2IrCl6 and 48 mg C6H8O7 were mixed in 5 mL deionized water to get 0.005 M Ir precursor solution. Then, the solution was stirred magnetically for 24 h at ambient temperature.
nodes.source_text: 11 mg (NH4)2IrCl6 and 48 mg C6H8O7 were mixed in 5 mL deionized water...

nodes.name: Citric acid-assisted impregnation-pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared MoO3/Ti was immersed into the above solution for 30 min. After being dried at 80°C for 5 min, the immersed MoO3/Ti was heated to 400°C at a heating rate of 10°C min^-1 in a muffle furnace in ambient atmosphere and kept for 5 h to finally obtain c-IrOx-MoO3/Ti.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show crystalline MoO3 (PDF#76-1003) and Ti (PDF#44-1294) phases for c-IrOx-MoO3/Ti and MoO3/Ti; no Ir oxide or metallic Ir signals detected due to low Ir loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Fig. 2a, X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of c- IrO_x MoO_3 / Ti and MoO_3 / Ti show two type of crystalline structures that could be assigned to the crystal phase of MoO3 PDF#76-1003) and Ti (PDF#44-1294), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of c-IrO_x-MoO_3/Ti show intertwined sheets with highly dispersed nanoparticles of 5–10 nm, different from fish-scale accumulative MoO3/Ti morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images of c-IrO_x -MoO_3/ Ti indicate that the fish-scale accumulative formation of the original MoO3/Ti is replaced completely by intertwined sheets, and highly dispersed nanoparticles with the size of about 5–10 nm are distributed on these sheets.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with circled features

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms intertwined MoO3 structure with IrOx nanoparticles in c-IrO_x-MoO_3/Ti; HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.326 nm (MoO3 (021)) and 0.256 nm (IrO2 (101)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM images of c-IrO_x -MoO_3/ Ti reveal two types of crystal plane spacings, i.e., 0.326 nm and 0.256 nm, which are further confirmed to belong to the planes of MoO3 (021) and IrO2 (101).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping show uniform distribution of Mo, O, Ir elements in c-IrO_x-MoO_3/Ti with Ir mass percentage close to 4 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM and EDS results of c-IrO_x -MoO_3/ Ti also indicate the uniform distribution of Mo, O, Ir elements in the samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman of c-IrO_x-MoO_3/Ti shows peaks from MoO3 (P_I ~820 cm⁻¹, P_II ~995 cm⁻¹), rutile IrO2 (E_g ~550 cm⁻¹, B_{2g} ~720 cm⁻¹), and amorphous IrO_x(OH)_y (α ~450 cm⁻¹, β ~605 cm⁻¹ with 30 cm⁻¹ red shift).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in the Raman spectra of c- IrO_x - MoO_3 / Ti, the markedly scattering peaks including α and β peaks originate from IrO_x(OH)_y, E_g and B_{2g} peaks from rutile IrO2, and P_I and P_II peaks as well as peaks at < 400 cm⁻¹ from MoO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of c-IrOx-MoO3/Ti: O1s peaks at 529.91 eV (lattice O), 530.55 eV (defective O ~40%), 532.17 eV (hydroxy O); Mo3d Mo⁶⁺/Mo⁵⁺ ratio 0.14 with Mo⁶⁺ shift to lower BE; Ir4f Ir³⁺/Ir⁴⁺ ratio 2.70 with Ir³⁺ shift +0.08 eV indicating MoO3-IrOx electronic interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The valence states of different elements in the catalysts are analyzed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). As shown in Fig. 3b, the O1s spectra of c- IrO_x - MoO_3 / Ti appears to have three peaks at 529.91 eV, 530.55 eV and 532.17 eV... These changes further confirm the electronic interaction between IrO_x and MoO_3.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES quantifies ultra-low Ir loading (<35 μg_Ir cm⁻²) and Ir content (<6 wt%) in catalytic layer; Mo content increases with deposition time.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mass concentrations of Ir and Mo in the obtained products with various position times are measured by ICP-OES (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of c-IrOx-MoO3/Ti shows MoO3 (021) 0.326 nm and IrO2 (101) 0.256 nm lattice spacings with blurry regions indicating amorphous IrOx; MoO3/Ti shows 0.326 nm (021), 0.381 nm (110), 0.265 nm (111) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the high-resolution TEM image of MoO3/Ti, three types of crystal plane spacings including 0.326 nm, 0.381 nm and 0.265 nm could be clearly observed which attribute to the (021), (110) and (111) planes of MoO3, respectively... The high-resolution TEM images of c-IrO_x -MoO_3/ Ti reveal two types of crystal plane spacings, i.e., 0.326 nm and 0.256 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX confirms elemental homogeneity; c-IrOx-MoO3/Ti shows ~4 wt% Ir; MoO3/Ti shows Mo/O ratio matching ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image as well as the elemental mapping results based on the energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) further prove that both Mo and O elements are uniformly distributed on MoO3/Ti... Notably, the extremely low mass percentage of Ir in c-IrO_x -MoO_3/ Ti (close to 4 wt%) implies a significant reduction of material cost for this catalyst.
